correctness.rationale: Effective resistance is a convex quadratic inverse form of the connected Laplacian, so price-preserving graph automorphism averaging maps any unrestricted connected feasible optimum to an orbit-constant optimum at the same or lower objective; positive full budget is used. For x matching weight, y other weight, the nonzero Laplacian eigenspaces have eigenvalues 2x+(2m-2)y and 2my. Matched and unmatched pair resistances are respectively 2/lambda_a and 1/lambda_a+1/lambda_b, exchanging maximality at t=x/y=1. Differentiating both scalar pieces gives thresholds r_-=2(m-1)/(2m-1), r=2 and t*=sqrt(m(m-1)(2/r-1))-(m-1) for r<r_-, t=1 for r_-<=r<2, t=0 for r>2 and continuum 0<=t<=1 at equality r=2. Substitution proves the three global minimum formulas; averaging and uniqueness within the symmetric scalar model prove universal matching-edge deletion for r>2 and forbid all-edge deletion for r<2, but do not assert unrestricted uniqueness. Independent exact rational full-matrix pseudoinverses for m=2..6 at several orbit weights agree with spectral resistance expressions; the lower critical-window expansion was checked symbolically.

originality.rationale: Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi (2008) contains the crucial convexity of effective resistance and explicitly lists minimization of maximum pair resistance as a convex SDP. Their analyzed graph families optimize total effective resistance and do not state the complete graph with a distinguished priced perfect matching or its exact 3-regime resistance-diameter solution. This claim credits the general method and adds explicit network-specific optimization and threshold/support laws.
residual_risks: An older network-specific minimax resistance analysis of complete graphs with a priced matching could express the same thresholds.
The theorem does not classify nonsymmetric minimizers and cannot be extended to edge caps or other price classes without new proof.

value.rationale: Minimax terminal-pair effective resistance is a natural robust electrical-network design objective under a linear budget. The complete analytical price phase diagram, equal-weight plateau despite unequal prices, deletion threshold P/Q=2 independent of graph size, and asymptotic scaling supply exact design guidance for an infinite family, not an arbitrary finite instance.

limitations: Only even cliques with a distinguished matching and two positive price classes; no unrestricted uniqueness claim.
Random feasible-sample comparisons are not an unrestricted optimality proof; convexity + averaging are.
